output.summary: KEP-2568 proposes running the kubeadm-managed control-plane components (kube-apiserver, kube-controller-manager, kube-scheduler, etcd) as non-root by setting runAsUser/runAsGroup, dropping capabilities, and setting the seccomp profile to runtime/default. Its status is implementable at alpha stage.
output.rationale: Running containers as root means a container escape can lead to root on the host, as CVE-2019-5736 showed. kubeadm is meant to provide a best-practice cluster setup, so the KEP applies the non-root practice to its control-plane pods. The KEP limits scope to control-plane components and excludes kubelet and kube-proxy.

alternatives.why_not: The design document states 'Alternatives: None' and gives no other options.

evidence.quote: If containers are running as root an escape from a container may result in the escalation to root in host.
`kubeadm` which is a tool built to provide a "best-practice" path to creating clusters is an ideal candidate to apply this to.
Run the control-plane components as non-root, by assigning a unique uid/gid to the containers in the Pods using the `runAsUser` and `runAsGroup` fields
Drop all but cap_net_bind_service from `kube-apiserver` Pod, this will allow us to run as non-root while still being able to bind to ports < 1024.
